content.text: {"core": "Abstraction lifts a thing into its pattern — strips the particulars, keeps the shape that repeats. In Wisdom, it works on the quiet inner knowing that already senses the whole before it names anything. Starved, the sensing stays wordless: what is felt never rises into a shape that can be held, weighed, or handed to another. The knowing stalls, mute.", "sheetLine": "The deep sense is there, but it never rises into a shape."}
